method: Static source/archive/trait evidence review, isolated OpenSSL decryption and gzip decoding only. No specimen executed or installed, and no sample endpoints contacted. Exact-hash prior native evidence is explicitly referenced.
scanner_comparison: Initial baseline uses the installed atomscan; final scan uses ../scan/target/release/atomscan and current traits. Additional extracted members come from pre-existing sibling engine improvements, not new engine changes made in this task.
training_policy: Claim only behavior supported by the artifact. No blanket hostility for job runners, opt-in/conditional telemetry, ordinary RMM capability or vulnerable-driver presence. Unknown payloads and provenance stay in purgatory. No attempt to inflate hostile-trait counts.

evidence: Emulated isolated native literal constructors: 1362 decoded outputs expose browser Login Data/cookies, wallets, cloud credential caches, .git-credentials, AI-tool configuration and CredentialManager output. Followed browser-pointer construction and collection/endpoint-string callers in disassembly. Added a narrow hostile composite for the actual profile-pointer array plus dense keyed literal builders.
limitations: No remote traffic or full application execution; not every collector/upload branch was fully recovered. VT 10 detections is corroboration, not the reason for this verdict.
Prior detailed evidence is reused by exact SHA256 and checked against the current source-built scan; no new native-code execution or emulation in this pass.

evidence: Universal macOS executable has masked arithmetic/LCG dispatch-state obfuscation and ad-hoc code-signature identity.
Existing control-flow obfuscation finding is accurate.
limitations: Protected native behavior remains unresolved; obfuscation or ad-hoc signing alone does not establish malware.

evidence: Unsigned Inno Setup loader claims VMware VMX Helper in version metadata and carries encrypted installer data.
Both available innoextract builds report an unsupported setup-data version and loader checksum mismatch.
limitations: Installer contents remain unresolved. A generic unpacking/checksum warning does not establish hostile behavior; do not infer malware from the collector filename.

evidence: Independently reconstructed the arithmetic-derived MD5 key, decrypted AES-128-CTR and decompressed the gzip payload without evaluating it.
Decoded stage uses octal-built curl/xattr/chmod commands to download into a hidden /tmp path, clear extended attributes, grant execution and launch the downloaded file.
Added a variable-bound encrypted-output/eval rule; unrelated eval and decrypt-only controls do not produce the hostile finding.
limitations: No endpoint contacted and no decoded stage or downloaded executable run.

evidence: Native PE exposes sparse system imports, repeated stack-table indirect calls and PE-header inspection observations.
Strings and current trait review did not recover an attack-specific payload.
limitations: Opaque native implementation is unresolved. No hostile rules manufactured from unsigned status, MZ constants or indirect calls alone.

evidence: Go executable has obfuscated identifiers and a self-issued Granite Sphere Group signature.
Current scan supports obfuscation, not a recovered credential-theft or command-and-control objective.
limitations: Renamed/garbled identifiers and self-signing do not settle intent. Payload behavior remains unresolved.

evidence: DLL contains repeated TLS reads and state-relative indirect-table dispatch, matching the existing flattening observation.
limitations: No injection, theft or command-and-control objective was independently recovered. Keep out of both good and bad training data until further reverse engineering.

evidence: Automatic bounded MPRESS LZMA recovery reproduces the independently recovered service/client hashes and scans the children. Bounded PE version-resource fallback recovers the client product claim despite the full parser resource-size guard. The remote-control implementation plus contradictory Disk Manager product identity triggers hostile on both client and wrapper. Earlier independent configuration decoding and Rizin analysis remain corroborating evidence.
limitations: No Grandoreiro family attribution or endpoint contact. Genuine RdViewer service remains neutral. Automatic recovery supports the recognized MPRESS x86 LZMA stub with explicit size/tree/depth limits, not every MPRESS variant.
Prior detailed evidence is reused by exact SHA256 and checked against the current source-built scan; no new native-code execution or emulation in this pass.

evidence: Source implements check-in/task/result HTTP protocol and dispatches externally supplied shell commands plus arbitrary file upload/download.
Encrypted local configuration, mesh peer configuration and screenshot dispatch accompany remote command tasking. Existing command-and-control findings describe those capabilities.
limitations: Explicit behavioral reconstruction with inert or absent main; harness supplies transport and capture. The offensive capability is present, but this is not claimed to be recovered deployed malware.

evidence: Same PE contains MeshCentral upstream implementation identity and a wss agent.ashx channel while VERSIONINFO claims Edge/msedge.exe.

Added a compound browser-product disguise finding; removing the product cover, implementation marker or channel defeats it.
limitations: No claim about the remote operator or successful deployment. Ordinary MeshCentral identity remains neutral.

evidence: Read all archive members and the complete postinstall command.
Postinstall generates a randomly named temporary package and invokes npm publish, then deletes the directory.
It writes a hardcoded token-shaped string into a local .npmrc; no extraction of victim credentials is present. Removed the unsupported credential-theft conviction.
printf fragments conceal the npm publish command word inside the install hook, supporting the existing concealed install-command finding.
limitations: No install hook executed and no registry request made. Publishing success and credential validity are unproven; a proof-of-concept name is not evidence of benign execution.

evidence: dist/heartbeat.js passes the complete process.env object into JSON.stringify in a fetch POST body.
README describes a small product/domain/version/status heartbeat and omits the full environment field.
The destination is supplied by the consuming caller. Tightened detection so body and POST/PUT/PATCH method must belong to the same fetch call.
limitations: Undocumented secret-bearing disclosure warrants suspicion; these bytes do not establish an attacker-controlled destination or intentional credential theft.

evidence: Go binary identifies itself as Zenconnekt Remote Support Agent and includes remote-support, screenshot, updater and certificate-install modules.
Signer metadata claims Acronis Web Suite through an Acronis-named CA; cryptographic consistency does not establish a trusted vendor root or authorized operator.
limitations: Remote-support functionality has legitimate uses. Neither benign vendor provenance nor a hostile deployment is established; no safety verdict based solely on a signer name.

evidence: Current source-built extraction exposes 57 scanned members of the single-file .NET application, instead of only its native host/runtime.
Recovered members carry hidden download/launch, reflective shellcode loading, browser app-bound key access, Discord LevelDB token/webhook theft and multi-application credential collection findings.
limitations: No payload executed. Installed scanner missing these children was a coverage limitation; no family attribution inferred from names.

evidence: Setup Factory archive exposes 160 scanned members, including a curl-export DLL with memory-execution loader evidence.
Other members include a kernel process killer and elevated MiniDump behavior; the fake-curl memory loader supplies the hostile attack evidence.
limitations: Legitimate libcurl/SQLite and installer support members are not individually labeled hostile. No payload executed and no family attribution derived from the collector filename.
